ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP (politically exposed persons) identification and enhanced due diligence under AMLA Art. 2 and AMLO-FINMA Art. 2; mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, beneficial owners and signatories against SECO consolidated embargo lists (implementing UNSC resolutions and Swiss autonomous sanctions), FINMA 'List of terrorist assets', OFAC SDN list (required for USD-denominated or U.S. payment rails), and EU/UK sanctions lists to the extent adopted or aligned by Switzerland; external counsel must document screening results in the pre-incorporation file, and any positive match triggers immediate enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification and Suspicious Activity Report to MROS.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Official Swiss Central Business Index (ZEFIX) at www.zefix.ch and the competent Cantonal Commercial Registry office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce / Registro di commercio)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Article 950 OR and the Commercial Register Ordinance (VRV/ORC), a company name must be submitted in a Swiss official language (German, French, Italian) or in a Latin-script transliteration; Romansh is permitted; the name cannot be misleading or imply false scope; a stock company (AG/SA/SA) must include 'Aktiengesellschaft' or 'AG' (or the French/Italian equivalents) unless a protected long-form is used; non-Latin scripts (e.g., Chinese characters) may appear in documentation but the registered name in ZEFIX must use the Latin alphabet.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Confederation / Bundesrat / Fédéral / Swiss / Suisse / Helvetia / Schweiz
Medical Device / Heilmittel (requires prior Swissmedic or cantonal licensing evidence)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Where a Cantonal Commercial Registry rejects a name, the applicant or its authorized agent may file a written objection for reconsideration with the competent Cantonal Commercial Registry within 10 days of the reasoned rejection. If reconsideration is denied, an administrative appeal must be lodged with the Cantonal Administrative Court (Verwaltungsgericht / Tribunal administratif) within 30 days of the written denial. A further appeal on grounds of violation of federal law may be made to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court (Bundesgericht) within 30 days of the cantonal appellate judgment. Parallel filings may use a materially revised name to avoid delay, and the reservation window may be extended for a further 30 days by paying the applicable cantonal fee before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office services may be used only as correspondence and administrative accommodation, but cannot constitute the sole registered office. The company must maintain a physical registered office in the place of the cantonal commercial register, capable of receiving official process and representatives. For a manufacturing scope under ISIC 3250, the authorities and Swissmedic require a demonstrable production or operation site in Switzerland; a pure virtual office is not acceptable for the statutory license or for the general anti-abuse substance test.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-high risk (approximately 40% probability) of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 24 months of operation. The likelihood is elevated because manufacturing of dental aligners is treated as a medical-device production activity requiring Swissmedic establishment licensing, cantonal health authority oversight, and ISO 13485 certification; inspections may occur without prior notice to verify actual personnel, equipment and processing of materials.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR), Arts. 620–763 (Aktiengesellschaft / Stock Company); Companies Register Ordinance (HRegV); Notarial Acts Act (Art. 9 OR).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce) of the canton of the registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public Deed of Incorporation (Errichtungserklärung) and Articles of Association (Statuten / Statuts), followed by the written application for entry in the Commercial Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: CHF 100,000 minimum share capital required for an AG; at least CHF 50,000 must be paid up in cash prior to registration via a blocked or escrow bank account. The bank's confirmation of capital liberation (Bankbescheinigung) must be submitted to the Commercial Register. Contributions in-kind are subject to sworn audit verification.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board of Directors, upon incorporation, unanimously resolves: (1) to acknowledge and accept the subscription of 1,000 registered shares with par value CHF 100.00 each, fully paid in accordance with the bank confirmation; (2) to adopt the registered office at the address stated in the Articles of Association and to authorize the submission of the incorporation dossier to the competent Commercial Register; (3) to appoint the directors named in the Articles and to entrust the chairperson with sole or joint signatory powers; (4) to open business bank accounts, appoint a fiduciary, and engage the statutory auditor if applicable; and (5) to grant full power to complete all statutory filings and obtain all operational permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal public notary (Zivilrechtsnotar / Notaire) with civil-law jurisdiction in the chosen canton.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed Articles of Association, the share subscription statement, and the identity documents of all founding shareholders and directors. The notary must authenticate the founders' signatures, confirm the capital structure, and execute the public deed before the Commercial Register filing.
required_dossiers: Passports or Swiss identity documents of all shareholders and directors
Draft Articles of Association (with indicated registered office, share capital, board powers, and signatory rules)
Share subscription declaration
Consent letters of appointed directors and signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries any inconsistency, correct the Articles or subscription documents and resubmit; no fee is refunded for an aborted deed, but a revised deed can be executed within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Capital Locked or Escrow Account and Obtaining the Capital Confirmation Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank (regulated by FINMA) or a licensed escrow agent for paid-up capital verification.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked/charter account in the company's name, deposit the minimum paid-in capital (CHF 50,000), and instruct the bank/escrow agent to issue a formal Capital Liberation Confirmation (Liberation Certificate) to be presented to the Commercial Register office.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association
Notarized deed of incorporation (if already issued)
Identity and UBO declarations of founding shareholders
Proof of initial deposit funds (source of funds form)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the deposit due to AML or documentation gaps, provide enhanced due diligence documents or select another licensed bank; alternatively use a notarial escrow account to hold funds until the bank opens its account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing for Incorporation with the Cantonal Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce) of the registered office canton.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic or signed registration application along with the notarial deed, Articles of Association, capital verification, and the declaration that all statutory requirements are fulfilled. The registry verifies legal compliance, approves entry, and assigns the company identification number (UID/EAN).
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation
Certified copy of the Articles of Association
Bank or escrow capital liberation certificate
Completed Commercial Register application form (including UBO declaration)
Confirmation of an available company name (name search)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency notice or query, provide the missing certified translations, corrected name reservation, or UBO amendments within the granted extension period; re-file within 10 business days to avoid rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Social Security and Prevention Institution Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV / FTA), cantonal tax office, and the responsible compensation office for AHV/AVS social security.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After Commercial Register entry, complete the tax registration questionnaire, register for VAT if taxable turnover exceeds the threshold (CHF 100,000 p.a. or liberal professions), and enroll with the social security (AHV/AVS) and accident insurance (SUVA) institutions. Obtain a VAT number and corporation tax account.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register excerpt (Handelsregisterauszug)
Articles of Association
Formular for VAT registration and tax enrollment
Board resolution appointing the responsible insurance representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office questions the projected turnover or status, revise the turnover declaration and submit supporting budgets; social security verifications can be cured by providing updated corporate details.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Swiss Official Gazette and Share Ledger Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the Commercial Register entry is completed, the registry ex officio instructs SHAB to publish the incorporation particulars. The company must establish its share ledger (Aktienbuch) listing shareholders, transfers, and pledges. The process is complete once the entry is final and the company is registered.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register certificate
Articles of Association
Shareholder registry data (UDO, nationality, share count)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SHAB publication contains errors, file a correction application to the Commercial Register and request a corrigendum; an updated excerpt is reissued within 2 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Swissmedic (Swiss Agency for Therapeutic Products) and the Cantonal Medical Devices Inspectorate for manufacturing operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Swissmedic Establishment Licence for Medical Devices (MedDO) — Manufacturing Authorization for Class I/IIa dental clear aligner and aligner sheet production.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / BAFU)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 'Registration and simple assessment' — no full EIA required provided VOC emissions are below 150 tonnes/year and no hazardous waste discharge is generated. If thermoforming involves chlorinated solvents or emissions exceed thresholds, the operation is reclassified as requiring an Environmental Impact Report.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater must comply with the Waters Protection Ordinance (GSchV) limits for COD, TSS, and pH; volatile organic compounds (VOCs) must meet the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV) threshold values for thermoforming processes using PETG, polypropylene and TPU; all plastic scrap and cleaning waste must be handled by licensed waste disposal operators under the Ordinance on the Movement of Waste (VEVA).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Mandatory fire safety clearance from the cantonal building and fire prevention authority, structural load inspection of the production floor, and occupational health/workplace authorization from SUVA (Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund) covering machine guarding, local exhaust ventilation and industrial noise exposure limits.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni AFC); official portal: www.estv.admin.ch; VAT registration portal: www.ezv.admin.ch (Federal Office for Customs and Border Security) and www.vat.admin.ch; e-services via the ESTV eService platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity or its Swiss branch/AG must first register with the Swiss commercial register (Handelsregister) at the cantonal level to obtain a Swiss company identification number (UID, Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer). For VAT purposes, the entity must then register with the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) by filing the VAT registration form (Registrierung für die Mehrwertsteuer) or through the electronic portal. Registration is mandatory if the entity conducts taxable activities in Switzerland and has annual worldwide turnover above CHF 100,000 for goods or services supplied in Switzerland, or if it supplies goods/services from abroad into Switzerland that are taxable in Switzerland and turnover exceeds CHF 100,000. The ESTV issues a separate VAT number (MWST-Nr / Numéro IDE / No IVA) distinct from the UID. Non-resident entities must appoint a Swiss fiscal representative domiciled in Switzerland to fulfill VAT filing and payment obligations if they are not established in Switzerland and have no Swiss residence or permanent establishment. The UID application must be submitted within 30 days of business commencement; the VAT registration application must be filed before the start of taxable activity or immediately upon exceeding the threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law does not provide an elective pass-through 'check-the-box' regime comparable to the US. However, the Swiss VAT Act provides an optional voluntary VAT registration election for businesses with turnover below CHF 100,000 (subject to irrevocable commitment of at least two years). Swiss entities may choose between ordinary VAT taxation and VAT group taxation (Mehrwertsteuergruppe) under Art. 20 of the Swiss VAT Act, allowing closely linked taxable persons to be treated as a single taxable entity. For corporate income tax, Swiss law provides statutory elections such as: (a) application of the Swiss participation relief (Beteiligungsabzug) for qualifying dividends and capital gains; (b) taxation under cantonal holding company or mixed company status in cantons that still grant such statuses; (c) reorganisations under the Swiss Merger Act, which require approval rather than unilateral election. Hybrid mismatch rules under Swiss law (Art. 8a VStG and implementing ordinances) do not contain an affirmative election; they merely deny deductions or recharacterize payments in cases of hybrid mismatch, but taxpayers may elect the ordering of rules within narrow statutory confines. Federal law does not allow a one-time elective deemed liquidation or step-up except for specific reorganisations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax / Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / Imposta sul valore aggiunto)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 in annual worldwide taxable turnover from goods supplied in Switzerland and services received or supplied in Switzerland, excluding exempt supplies and investment gold; a separate lower threshold of CHF 100,000 applies for non-established foreign suppliers. There is no separate threshold for e-commerce marketplace operators; platform suppliers are jointly liable under special rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not currently operate a real-time fiscal clearance or continuous transaction control (CTC) model requiring pre-clearance approval by the tax authority before issuance. Electronic invoicing is permitted under the ordinary VAT invoice rules if the invoice contains all statutory data fields, authenticity of origin, integrity of content, and legibility are ensured. The recognised e-invoicing standard is the Swiss e-invoice format (Peppol BIS-based, XML/UBL 2.1, or Swiss-specific formats such as Swico or EBill for consumer billing). From 1 January 2024, Swiss payment invoices must display a QR code (QR-IBAN) for domestic B2B and B2C invoices in CHF; for non-CHF and foreign transactions, the old payment slip can still be used. There is no mandatory digital stamping or fiscal seal. Invoices must be retained for 10 years. The Swiss VAT Act requires issuance of a VAT invoice for B2B supplies above CHF 400 (invoice amount incl. VAT) with full data set; for B2C, a simplified invoice is sufficient below CHF 400. There is an obligation to file electronically (VAT return via eService or Swissdec-certified software) for businesses with turnover above CHF 100,000; no periodic real-time data submission to the tax authority is required before the filing deadline.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The export of tangible movable goods to foreign destinations is zero-rated (tax rate 0%) under Art. 23(1) and Art. 53 of the Swiss VAT Act, provided the supplier can prove that the goods were transported abroad within a statutory deadline and that the foreign consignee is the acquirer. The supply qualifies if the goods are actually exported by the supplier, the recipient, or a third party instructed by the recipient, and if the destination is abroad (not a Swiss customs exclusion zone like Samnaun). Services related to exported goods (e.g., transport, handling) and certain cross-border services (including intellectual property licences, services to foreign recipients that are not used in Switzerland) are also zero-rated under Art. 23(2) and Art. 53 VAT Act if the recipient's registered seat or residence is abroad. For sales via marketplace/Stripe, the supplier must identify the place of supply in accordance with Art. 7-8 VAT Act: goods placed in Switzerland and shipped abroad qualify as export when the transport begins in Switzerland and ends in a foreign country. Dental aligners manufactured and sold by a Swiss AG to foreign orthodontists are zero-rated if shipped to a non-Swiss address and properly declared. The refund of input VAT is only possible for export business via the VAT return (negative VAT position), subject to the general right to deduct input tax under Art. 28-32 VAT Act; alternatively, non-established foreign entities may claim a VAT refund under the Swiss VAT refund procedure (Form 30) for taxes borne on goods/services purchased in Switzerland, subject to reciprocity.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss Customs Export Declaration (Exportdeklaration / Exportmeldung via NCTS or e-dec system) with customs transit document (T1, T2 or ATS-G) or proof of exit (Ausgangsbescheinigung)
Commercial invoice with Swiss VAT zero-rating notation (e.g., '0% MWST Export') and seller's Swiss UID/VAT number and buyer's foreign VAT ID
Bill of Lading (B/L) or airway bill (AWB) / CMR (international consignment note) / postal dispatch receipt showing consignee abroad
Proof of transport: signed contract of carriage (CMR full set), freight invoice, or certificate of shipment by logistics provider
Inward Remittance Certificate / Bank statement showing payment from the foreign buyer (foreign exchange repatriation evidence)
Proof of export from Swiss customs: stamped export document (Ausfuhrschein / bordereau d'exportation / bollettino d'esportazione) or electronic export confirmation from the e-dec/NCTS system
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Swiss Federal Tax Administration scrutinises zero-rated export supplies with substantive documentary requirements. If the exporter fails to prove export within the statutory time limits, the supply is recharacterised as domestic taxable at the standard rate, and VAT is newly assessed with interest. Penalties: tax evasion (Hinterziehung) under Art. 69 Swiss VAT Act: penalty up to 3 times the tax evaded; simple violation under Art. 70: admonition or fine up to CHF 8,000; violation of bookkeeping and other obligations under Art. 66-68: fines up to CHF 5,000 (severe cases up to CHF 10,000). For fraudulent export zero-rating, criminal penalties under the Swiss Criminal Code and Art. 186-188 VAT Act apply, including imprisonment up to 5 years. A retrospective clawback can extend 10 years for tax evasion; the ordinary limitation is 5 years for simple VAT assessments. The exporter must retain export documents for 10 years; failure to produce documentary evidence leads to denial of zero-rating and reassessment at 8.1% or the applicable reduced rate. Additionally, customs penalties under the Administrative Penalty Act (2019) may impose fines up to CHF 20,000 and confiscation of goods for false declarations or misclassification. The Federal Supreme Court requires bona fide commercial substance and proof of physical movement; circular transactions or shell intermediaries will be challenged as abusive.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB); supervision of banks and financial market infrastructure is exercised by the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority FINMA (Eidgenössische Finanzmarktaufsicht). The legal framework is the Federal Act on Currency and Payment Instruments, the Banking Act of 1934 (as amended), and FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full capital and current account convertibility for the Swiss franc. There are no foreign exchange controls, no mandatory surrender of export proceeds, no central bank approval for cross-border transfers, and no restrictions on the conversion of CHF into other currencies. Foreign investors may inject equity and debt capital freely, and a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft may remit dividends, interest, royalties, or service fees abroad without prior exchange administration clearance. The only substantive remittance hurdle is tax-related: dividends and similar profit distributions attract Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) at 35%, recoverable or reduced if the beneficial owner qualifies for a double-taxation treaty relief, the Swiss domestic participation exemption, or a Swiss parent-subsidiary mechanism. Interest on arm's-length loans, commercial trade payments, and salaries may be paid cross-border without withholding tax provided the recipient is not subject to Swiss fiduciary obligations. The CHF itself is fully convertible, and pricing and invoicing may be denominated in CHF, EUR, USD, or any agreed currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory obligation in Switzerland requiring exporters to surrender export proceeds to the SNB or to convert foreign currency receipts into CHF. Export proceeds may remain in freely convertible foreign currency accounts at Swiss banks or be credited to any foreign bank account at the discretion of the Swiss exporter. The Swiss franc is freely floating under a flexible exchange-rate policy driven by the SNB's monetary policy. No mandatory conversion ratio, repatriation deadline, or FINMA approval applies to export receipts. Export transactions are nevertheless subject to ordinary anti-money-laundering and sanctions compliance, and the receiving bank must be able to identify the commercial underlying, the beneficial owner, and the source of funds in the event of unusual patterns. For Swiss value-added tax purposes, export proceeds are generally treated as zero-rated supplies, but the tax status has no effect on FX surrender obligations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium. Switzerland is not a member of the EEA, so an offshore Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licensed in the UK, Lithuania, or Singapore cannot benefit from an EU payment-services passport in Switzerland. An offshore EMI wishing to offer account or payment services to a Swiss AG must rely on a Swiss-licensed partner bank for SIC and SEPA settlement or obtain a Swiss FinTech authorization under Article 1b of the Swiss Banking Act, limited to deposits not exceeding CHF 100 million and subject to FINMA supervision. For a low-risk dental aligner manufacturer, a reputable Swiss Tier-1 bank remains more practical and cheaper than a FinTech EMI because of the company's need for documentary trade facilities, Swiss franc clearing through SIC, and credible banking counterparty status for international orthodontic distributors. Offshore digital EMIs are feasible only as a supplementary payment channel for marketplace collections and are not recommended as the primary treasury bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Swiss anti-money-laundering rules permit remote video identification of directors and beneficial owners using FINMA-recognised identity-verification procedures (FINMA Circular 2016/07). In practice, Swiss resident directors can open accounts fully remotely if the bank accepts video KYC, but a newly incorporated AG with non-resident shareholders, high-value capital contributions, or complex UBO structures will normally be required to perform at least one physical or notarial identity interview at a Swiss branch or with a Swiss notary public. The onboarding process typically requires the chairman, CEO, or beneficial owner to appear in person at the bank's premises for the signature profile if account signatories are foreign natural persons. A Swiss-registered company can mitigate this by appointing a local executive signatory for the operational account while keeping foreign UBO identity checks to a documented notarial appointment in Switzerland. Where the entity is wholly foreign-owned, the bank may request a sworn declaration from the UBO's local bank confirming source of wealth and source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dissociated ownership with non-resident UBO holding 100% of the CHF 100,000 minimum share capital and no prior relationship with Swiss financial institutions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified commercial register extract, articles of incorporation, notarised minutes of the shareholders' meeting approving the share capital, UBO declaration forms, passport and residence permits of all directors and shareholders, bank reference letters from the UBO's home-country bank, source-of-wealth reports, audited financial statements if any, and a clear written explanation of the capital payment origin, including the account from which the CHF transfer is initiated and the economic link between the UBO and the dental aligner vertical.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction volume from e-commerce platforms, Stripe, and third-party marketplace aggregators collecting patient payments and orthodontic clinic fees.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed contractual framework showing the role of each platform as a payment collection agent, end-user terms and privacy notices, clinic onboarding agreements, reconciliation reports, transaction-level source data for chargebacks and refunds, and a documented AML risk assessment for the clear aligner business demonstrating that product sales are tangible medical-device supplies with low money-laundering vulnerability.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving countries listed as high-risk or monitored by FATF, or involving convertible-currency settlement through UAE, Hong Kong, or Singapore trust accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full supply-chain documentation, commercial contracts and invoices, bills of lading and airway bills, UCP600-compliant letters of credit, customs declarations, tax identification numbers of the counterparty, an economic-substance explanation, and an internal sanctions screening log proving that all counterparties are not persons subject to Swiss OFAC-compatible restricting measures or EU/UN sanctions adopted by Switzerland.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual source of funds as cash deposits, digital-asset holdings, foreign crypto exchange transfers, or private loans from unrelated third parties intended to capitalise or credibly prefinance the Swiss AG.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Swiss notarial deed evidencing the loan or capital increase, loan agreements, proof of the lender's identity and licensed-custodian records, a digital-asset tax statement if applicable, a certified AML/KYC file from the lending institution, a certificate of domicile, and sworn declaration that no third party holds a beneficial interest or voting rights without disclosure under the Swiss Code of Obligations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The initial share capital of CHF 100,000 for an AG must be paid into a blocked or escrow account in the name of the company before the commercial register registrar will issue the certificate of incorporation. The chosen Swiss bank will provide a capital-escrow deposit confirmation, and the subscription proceeds must come from a verifiable bank account in the name of the shareholder or, if the contribution is made by a third party, with a written designated-funds declaration stating the underlying capital relationship. All wires must be sent via SWIFT MT103 using the bank's own settlement identity, with the remitter field matching the shareholder's name and the further-credits field clearly identifying the Swiss AG. The Swiss bank will require the original or certified copy of the notary's capital-payment attestation and will perform an onward transfer of funds to the company's operational account only after the commercial register entry is effected. No foreign-exchange declaration or SNB approval is required, but the payment reference should be 'Sacheinlage / contribuciòn de capital' or 'Share capital contribution – AG incorporation', and the source-of-funds documentation must be retained for ten years under Swiss AML obligations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The Swiss AG will clear trade disbursements primarily through the SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) system, SEPA (if settling in EUR within the EEA), and SWIFT MT103 messages for cross-border settlement with USD, CNY, or other convertible currencies. Export shipments of dental clear aligner sheets and custom-formed trays are settled by irrevocable documentary letters of credit (L/C) in favour of the Swiss company, by L/C for the Swiss company's own purchases of PETG copolymers and automated trimming equipment, or by telegraphic transfer with clean payment terms. For commercial L/C transactions, the issuing bank forwards SWIFT MT700 messages to the Swiss advising bank, and the Swiss beneficiary presents compliant documents (commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, airway bill/bill of lading, sanitary and MEDDEV attestations if required) for payment through the accepting bank. Reduced export risk is achieved by using confirmed irrevocable L/Cs subject to UCP600, particularly where distributors in emerging markets are involved. For direct disbursements to suppliers, the Swiss AG should use only authenticated corporate internet channels with dual authorisation, always include the bank-approved purpose code (e.g., 'Goods - medical devices'), and maintain commercial contracts with supporting shipping documents to satisfy account relationship reviews and compliance screenings.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward FX contracts with a Swiss licensed credit institution or its group treasury
Standard FX swaps for simultaneous spot and forward settlement
Vanilla foreign currency options (call/put on EUR, USD, CNY and CHF)
Barrier options and structured forward packages approved by the bank's derivatives desk
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CIRS) for non-CHF local currency borrowing
FX futures traded on regulated EU and Swiss exchanges where the Swiss bank acts as clearing member
Nondeliverable forwards (NDFs) if the counterparty bank applies this instrument to manage convertibility restrictions on a settlement currency, though not required for CHF
FX participation forwards and plain-vanilla asset swaps used only for hedging underlying procurement and distribution exposure, not for speculative treasury operations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Joint Federal, Cantonal and Municipal Corporate Income Tax Return (Federal Statement, Cantonal Statement and Municipal Statement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (e.g., Zug Department of Finance) and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) via the national e-tax portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Typically due 3–6 months after the balance sheet date; for a 31 December year-end, the return is generally filed by 31 May or 30 June, with extensions of up to 6 months available upon written request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late interest at 4.5% per annum; administrative penalty for late filing up to 25% of the assessed tax; if the return is omitted, the tax authority estimates the taxbase (Sicherheitszuschlag) and may impose a fine up to CHF 10,000

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT Return (where an annual VAT settlement period has been elected under the Swiss VAT Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after expiry of the annual tax period; for a 31 December year-end, due by 1 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission penalty of CHF 100–200 per return; default interest at 4.5% per annum; intentional tax evasion carries a fine of up to 3 times the VAT evaded

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Social Security Wage Declaration (LONA/LaNa) including AHV/AVS, ALV, NBUV, and FAK contributions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Compensation Fund of the registered office (AHV-Ausgleichskasse) and, where applicable, the SVA (cantonal social insurance authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March following the calendar year in which the wages were paid, or such later date as the compensation fund may grant on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to CHF 30,000 for late or incomplete submission; 5% default interest on overdue contributions; criminal penalties for willful misreporting (fine up to CHF 20,000)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Internal Annual Confirmation and Update of the Share Register and Minutes Book (including changes in Shareholders, Directors and UBOs recorded in the Aktienregister)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No filing to a government body; records retained at the registered office and produced to the Commercial Register Office, tax authorities, or FINMA on lawful request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing upon each share transfer; final verification and approval at the Annual General Meeting, which must be held within six months after the balance sheet date (typically by 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Direct civil liability for board members; non-compliance with inspection rights may trigger regulatory fines up to CHF 5,000 and, in serious cases, a strike-off order from the Commercial Register after due process

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An ordinary (full) audit is required if the company exceeds any two of the following for two consecutive fiscal years: CHF 20 million balance sheet total, CHF 40 million annual revenue, 250 full-time employees on average. A limited (review) audit is required if the company exceeds any two of: CHF 2 million balance sheet total, CHF 10 million annual revenue, 10 full-time employees. If the company falls below the limited-audit criteria, shareholders may resolve to opt out of any audit provided no threshold is met and the company has fewer than 10 employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Articles 957–963) with Swiss GAAP FER permitted; IFRS is allowed but not mandatory for unlisted companies. Listed companies must apply IFRS or Swiss GAAP FER with additional listing rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law does not require a public UBO filing for a non-regulated AG. The company must maintain an internal register of ultimate beneficial owners (Art. 697j CO) and update it no later than the end of the business day following any acquisition or transfer of shares that changes UBO status. An annual internal verification must be carried out before the AGM; no communication to the authorities is required unless the company is a financial intermediary under FinIA, in which case FINMA and the Anti-Money Laundering Authority receive annual confirmation and audit reports.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minutes Book of Shareholders' and Board of Directors' Meetings
Accounting Records, Financial Statements and Business Correspondence

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% (federal corporate income tax; cantonal and communal taxes apply, effective combined rate typically 12–20% depending on canton)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Patent box regime (reduced taxation of qualifying IP income), R&D super deduction (150% of eligible R&D expenses), notional interest deduction on excess equity, and participation relief for substantial shareholdings. For dental aligner manufacturing, R&D incentives and patent box may apply to innovative aligner materials and processes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss corporate tax return (Steuererklärung / Déclaration fiscale) filed via the cantonal tax authority's electronic portal (e.g., eTax, VST, or the federal ePortal for federal tax). The federal tax return is integrated into the cantonal return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally due within 6 months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., for a 31 December year-end, filing by 30 June of the following year). Extensions may be granted upon request, but interest accrues on late payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, UID (business identification number), and fiscal year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with a Swiss permanent establishment (PE) must file a separate return for the PE, using the same form and indicating the PE's Swiss address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue, cost of goods sold, operating expenses, and net profit before tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate income and expenses to the Swiss PE based on arm's length principles; provide transfer pricing documentation if intercompany transactions exceed thresholds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses (e.g., excessive director fees, bribes), deduction of tax-exempt income (e.g., participation dividends), and application of patent box or R&D deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must ensure that adjustments are consistent with the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines and Swiss tax law; maintain contemporaneous documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Equity capital, reserves, and retained earnings as per statutory balance sheet.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a PE, report the capital attributable to the PE; ensure compliance with thin capitalization rules (debt-to-equity ratio).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of federal, cantonal, and communal taxes based on taxable profit and applicable rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents are subject to federal tax on Swiss-source income; cantonal and communal taxes may apply if the PE is in a specific canton.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of any Swiss withholding tax on dividends, interest, or royalties paid to non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the company is a Swiss entity, report distributions and apply for treaty relief; if the company is non-resident, report any Swiss-source income subject to WHT.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: CHF 100–5,000 per month of delay (cantonal variations). Interest on unpaid tax accrues at 3–5% per annum. Intentional tax evasion may result in fines up to 3 times the evaded tax and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% (statutory Swiss withholding tax on dividends paid to non-residents; reduced to 0% for qualifying Swiss parent companies under participation relief, and to 0–15% under applicable DTA).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident recipient must obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from their home tax authority and submit it to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA) via the 'Form 823' (for dividends) or 'Form 824' (for interest/royalties) before the payment is made. The FTA may grant a refund of excess WHT or a direct exemption if the conditions are met. The process typically takes 4–8 weeks.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: No Swiss withholding tax on royalties (unless they are considered as income from immovable property). Interest: 35% statutory WHT on interest from Swiss sources (e.g., bonds, bank deposits), but interest on ordinary commercial loans between related companies is exempt if the lender is not a Swiss resident and the loan is not structured as a taxable bond. Under DTAs, interest WHT is typically reduced to 0–10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File required if the group's consolidated revenue exceeds CHF 50 million and the value of intercompany transactions exceeds CHF 5 million (per transaction type). For smaller entities, a simplified documentation (Contemporaneous TP Study) is recommended.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not have a formal Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) like the UAE, but the Federal Act on the Tax Treatment of Holding Companies and the Participation Relief require that a company have genuine economic substance (e.g., employees, premises, and decision-making) to benefit from participation relief or treaty benefits. The OECD's Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) actions, particularly Action 5, require substantial activity for IP holding companies. For a dental aligner manufacturer, substance is evidenced by R&D, production, and management activities in Switzerland.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of income, false documentation, or concealment of taxable profits in Swiss or foreign accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to 3 times the evaded tax (federal and cantonal), plus interest. Criminal prosecution may lead to imprisonment up to 3 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers can be held personally liable for tax evasion if they knowingly participated or failed to act. Civil restitution of evaded taxes, travel bans, and potential extradition under mutual legal assistance treaties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a letterbox company without real business activities, employees, or premises, while claiming treaty benefits or holding IP solely for tax avoidance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, reclassification of income, and imposition of 35% withholding tax on deemed distributions. Fines up to CHF 100,000 for non-compliance with substance requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid withholding taxes and penalties if they knowingly facilitated the shell structure. Travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement adequate anti-money laundering controls, or involvement in transactions linked to proceeds of crime (e.g., fraudulent billing, corruption).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines up to CHF 500,000 for the company, and imprisonment for individuals. Regulatory sanctions include revocation of licenses and exclusion from public procurement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can face imprisonment up to 5 years and personal fines. Civil liability for damages to third parties. Travel bans and asset seizures are common.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain arm's length pricing for intercompany transactions (e.g., sale of aligner sheets to related distributors at non-market prices) or failure to file TP documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, penalties of 20–50% of the additional tax assessed, and interest. In severe cases, criminal prosecution for tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for the additional tax if they approved the non-arm's length pricing. Travel bans and professional disqualification may apply.
